## Uncertainty analysis.

The large variability of seismic hazard must be considered in design scenarios with a high degree of consequences to failure. The PSHA study prepared by LCI, has reported seismic intensities and annual exceedance probabilities for seven fractiles (5%, 10%, 16%, 50%, 84%, 90% and 5%) that allow estimating the variability of seismic hazard for a given service level. Assuming a log-normal distribution $ln(X) \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_{lnX},\,\sigma_{lnX}^{2})$ for the seismic intensities of a given service level, the dispersion between the 16% and 84% percentiles allows estimating the standard error of the hazard model, according to $\sigma_{lnX} \approx 1/2 \ log ({X_{84\%}}/{X_{16\%}})$ and the mean value $\mu_{lnX} \approx \frac{1}{2} \left( log(X_{84\%}) + log(X_{16\%}) \right)$. 

If $\eta_X=exp(\mu_{lnX})$ is the median (50%) of some seismic intensity measure, the 84% percentile of this measure can be estimated from $X_{84\%} \approx \eta_X \ exp(\sigma_{lnX})$ and this expression can be used to estimate the variability of any seismic design parameter based on that intensity measure, assuming that they have a log-normal distribution and an approximately linear relationship with the seismic intensity. The following table presents the standard error $\sigma_{X}=exp(\sigma_{lnX})$ for different service levels (return periods), based on 16% and 84% estimates for $S_a(T_n)$ 



```{r include=TRUE}
#| label: tbl-T2
#| fig-cap: Standard Error $\sigma_{lnX}$ for PGA at different service levels
DT <-  UHSTable[SM=="aep"][ p %in%  c(0.16,0.84) & Vs30==760 ,.(AEP,Tn,p,Sa)] |> unique()
DT16 <- DT[p==0.16,.(AEP,Tn,Sa16=Sa)] 
DT84 <- DT[p==0.84,.(AEP,Tn,Sa84=Sa)] 
AUX <- DT84[DT16,on=.(AEP,Tn)] #merge(DT16,DT84,by=c("TR","Tn"),all=TRUE) |> na.omit()
AUX[,sigmaLnX:=round(0.5*(log(Sa84)-log(Sa16)),digits = 4),by=.(Tn,AEP)]
DT <- AUX[DT,on=.(Tn,AEP)] #merge(DT,AUX,by=.(Tn,TR,Vs30),all=TRUE) |> na.omit()
DATA <- DT[,.(ID=1/AEP,Y=exp(sigmaLnX),X=Tn)]|> unique()
setorder(DATA,X)
buildPlot::buildPlot(
  library="hc",
  color.palette = "Dynamic",
  yAxis.label =TRUE,
  plot.type="line",
  legend.layout="horizontal",
  legend.show=FALSE,
  xAxis.log = FALSE,
  yAxis.log = FALSE,
  xAxis.legend="Tn[s]",
  yAxis.legend="sigma[g]",
  data=DATA)

```
